```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>"
)
options(ABCatlas.download_progress = FALSE)
```

`ABCatlas` provides an R-native, release-aware interface to the
[Allen Brain Cell (ABC)
Atlas](https://portal.brain-map.org/atlases-and-data/bkp/abc-atlas).

The ABC Atlas, from the Allen Institute, brings together whole-brain
single-cell, single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics datasets from the
mouse, human, macaque and marmoset brain, together with their cell type
taxonomies. Its H5AD expression matrices and CSV metadata files are
distributed through a public Amazon S3 bucket that requires no account.
`ABCatlas` lets R users find these datasets, select cells and genes from
their metadata, check the size of a request before downloading, and read
the selected expression into R.

The package separates metadata discovery and cell selection from
expression transfer:

1.  `list_datasets()` discovers curated dataset routes.
2.  `load_data()` assembles metadata and selects cells.
3.  `plan_fetch()` previews the expression request and required files.
4.  `fetch_data()` reads selected expression into the requested R
    representation.

## Installation

Install the package with `BiocManager`:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("ABCatlas")
```

Then load it:

```{r library}
library(ABCatlas)
```

Core metadata and matrix functionality is R-native. The primary output is a
sparse matrix bundle. SingleCellExperiment and SpatialExperiment outputs
are available directly as alternative representations.

## Discovering datasets

Use `list_datasets()` to inspect the curated routes supported by the
package:

```{r list-datasets}
datasets <- list_datasets()
datasets
```

The catalog reports each route's modality, spatial and imputed status,
default representation and available expression representations.

It is also an ordinary data frame:

```{r spatial-datasets}
datasets[datasets$spatial, ]
```

`list_datasets()` reads the package registry only and performs no
network access.

## Loading metadata

`load_data()` loads and assembles cell and gene metadata. It does not
fetch the large expression matrices.

This vignette uses `Zhuang4`, one of four MERFISH datasets from Zhang et
al. (2023). It covers three sagittal sections of an adult mouse brain
measured with a 1,122-gene panel, and its cells are mapped to the whole
mouse brain taxonomy of Yao et al. (2023). The ABC Atlas distributes the
approximately 0.16 million cells that passed the mapping confidence
threshold. Its metadata take about 40 MB and its raw expression about
64 MB.

```{r load-data}
abc <- load_data("Zhuang4")
abc
```

The cell metadata hold one row per cell, with anatomical, donor and
taxonomy annotations and, for this spatial route, the `x`, `y` and `z`
coordinates:

```{r cell-metadata}
head(abc$cell_metadata)
```

The gene metadata hold one row per gene, keyed by `gene_identifier`:

```{r gene-data}
head(abc$gene_data)
```

`unique_values` lists the values found in the main metadata columns,
which can be used as cell filters. The number of values per column and
the first few of each:

```{r unique-values}
lengths(abc$unique_values)
lapply(abc$unique_values, head, n = 3)
```

## Selecting cells and genes

Cell selection can be performed during `load_data()` so that the cells
included in the analysis are defined before expression data are
requested. Genes are selected when the expression is planned and
fetched. The cells and genes below are taken from the outputs shown in
the previous section.

### Cell selection

`filters` is a named list in which each name is a metadata column and
each value specifies which cells to retain. Cells must match every
filter, and any of the values within one filter. Here, brain section
`Zhuang-ABCA-4.002` and the GABAergic and glutamatergic cells in it:

```{r cell-selection}
filters <- list(
    brain_section_label = "Zhuang-ABCA-4.002",
    neurotransmitter = c("GABA", "Glut")
)
abc_filtered <- load_data("Zhuang4", filters = filters)
nrow(abc_filtered$cell_metadata)
table(abc_filtered$cell_metadata$neurotransmitter)
```

When the desired cells are already known, `cell_ids` selects those exact
cell labels. Here, the first three cells of `head(abc$cell_metadata)`:

```{r cell-id-selection}
my_cell_labels <- head(abc$cell_metadata$cell_label, 3)
abc_exact <- load_data("Zhuang4", cell_ids = my_cell_labels)
abc_exact$cell_metadata[, c("brain_section_label", "subclass")]
```

When the filtered population is still large, `n_cells` limits the number
of cells returned. Use `seed` when the subset should be reproducible:

```{r cell-sampling}
abc_sampled <- load_data(
    "Zhuang4",
    filters = filters,
    n_cells = 1000,
    seed = 42
)
nrow(abc_sampled$cell_metadata)
```

### Gene selection

Expression rows are keyed by canonical `gene_identifier`. Each requested
gene is matched first against `gene_identifier`, then against the
published source identifier, then against `gene_symbol`, so symbols and
identifiers can be mixed. Here, three genes from `head(abc$gene_data)`
by symbol and Rxrg by its identifier:

```{r gene-selection}
genes <- c("Htr7", "Sema3c", "Itga8", "ENSMUSG00000015843")
abc$gene_data[
    abc$gene_data$gene_symbol %in% genes |
        abc$gene_data$gene_identifier %in% genes,
    c("gene_identifier", "gene_symbol")
]
```

## Planning expression access

Expression files can be several gigabytes. Before downloading them,
inspect the request with `plan_fetch()`:

```{r plan-fetch}
plan <- plan_fetch(abc_filtered, genes = genes)
plan
```

A fetch plan reports:

-   the resolved ABC Atlas release;
-   the published representation (`raw` or `log2`);
-   requested genes and cells;
-   expression files involved;
-   selected-file sizes;
-   whether each file is cached;
-   resumable partial bytes;
-   additional download required.

`plan_fetch()` does not download expression matrices.

In an interactive R session, `plan_fetch()` asks
`Proceed with download? [y/n]:`. Answering `y` approves the plan, and
`fetch_data(plan = plan)` then downloads and reads what was planned.
Answering `n` discards the plan, and the request must be planned again
before fetching. In this vignette the question is answered with `y`.

The legacy `metadata =` and `gene_data =` arguments remain available,
but the `abc_data` interface is preferred because it carries routing and
release provenance automatically.

## Fetching expression

`fetch_data()` downloads the expression files the selection needs, then
reads only the selected cells and genes:

```{r fetch-matrix}
x <- fetch_data(
    abc_filtered,
    genes = genes,
    return_type = "matrix" # could pick "sce" or "spatial"
)
dim(x$expression)
x$expression[, 1:3]
Matrix::rowSums(x$expression > 0)
x$provenance
```

This returns an `abc_matrix` object containing sparse expression,
selected metadata and provenance. Rows are genes, keyed by
`gene_identifier`, and columns are cells;
`Matrix::rowSums(x$expression > 0)` counts the selected cells in which
each gene is detected. The provenance records the dataset, release,
representation, modality, spatial status and selected dimensions.

Depending on the downstream analysis, choose `data_type = "raw"` for
raw counts or `data_type = "log2"` for the log2-transformed values
published by the ABC Atlas. `list_datasets()` shows the default and
available representations of each route. Each representation is a
separate file, so only one is downloaded: this request used the
`Zhuang4` default, `raw`.

## Output representations

`return_type` selects the representation returned by `fetch_data()`:

-   `"matrix"`, the primary output, is the sparse matrix bundle shown
    above.
-   `"sce"` returns a SingleCellExperiment. Raw expression uses a
    `counts` assay. Upstream transformed expression uses a `log2` assay.
-   `"spatial"` returns a SpatialExperiment with the spatial coordinates
    attached. Automatic coordinate inference is restricted to routes
    declared spatial, such as `Zhuang4`. For other metadata, verified
    coordinate columns must be supplied explicitly with
    `coordinate_columns`.

SingleCellExperiment and SpatialExperiment objects store the provenance
in object metadata, and SpatialExperiment provenance additionally
records the coordinate columns used.

Seurat and Monocle 3 objects are not built by `ABCatlas`. Users of
either tool can convert the matrix output with the code below, which
needs the `SeuratObject` package (CRAN) or the `monocle3` package
(GitHub). Both tools expect count data, so use raw expression; `x` above
is raw.

```{r convert-seurat-monocle3, eval=FALSE}
# Seurat: Seurat replaces "_" in feature names, so rename them first.
counts <- x$expression
rownames(counts) <- gsub("_", "-", rownames(counts))
seu <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = counts,
    meta.data = x$cell_metadata
)

# Monocle 3: gene metadata need a gene_short_name column.
gene_metadata <- x$gene_data
gene_metadata$gene_short_name <- gene_metadata$gene_symbol
cds <- monocle3::new_cell_data_set(
    x$expression,
    cell_metadata = x$cell_metadata,
    gene_metadata = gene_metadata
)
```

## Reusing cached data

Downloaded files are reused from the local cache. Planning the same
request again shows that nothing needs to be downloaded, so the plan is
approved automatically:

```{r reuse-plan}
plan_again <- plan_fetch(abc_filtered, genes = genes)
plan_again$total_download
plan_again$approved
```

Because it is approved, the plan can be passed to `fetch_data()`. The
expression file is read from the cache, and the message reports that no
download was needed:

```{r reuse-fetch}
x_again <- fetch_data(plan = plan_again)
identical(x$expression, x_again$expression)
```

Other datasets use the same cache. `HMBA_PatchSeq` holds 717 Patch-seq
cells from macaque striatum, part of the Human and Mammalian Brain Atlas
(HMBA) basal ganglia data. Patch-seq combines patch-clamp
electrophysiology with single-cell RNA sequencing; these cells are mapped
to striatal neuron types of the HMBA basal ganglia taxonomy. The dataset
is not spatial and is published only as `log2` expression, which is
therefore its default representation:

```{r second-dataset}
patch_seq <- load_data("HMBA_PatchSeq")
patch_seq
```

```{r second-fetch}
y <- fetch_data(patch_seq, genes = c("GAD1", "PPP1R1B", "DRD1", "DRD2"))
dim(y$expression)
y$data_type
```

## Cache location and releases

ABC Atlas metadata and expression files can be large. Files are
downloaded once and reused from a local cache.

The cache directory is resolved in this order:

1.  explicit `download_base`;
2.  `options(ABCatlas.download_base = ...)`;
3.  the `ABC_ATLAS_CACHE` environment variable;
4.  a per-user package cache directory.

For example, `options(ABCatlas.download_base = "~/ABCatlas-cache")` keeps
the cache in a folder of your home directory.

The package is release-aware. A release can be pinned explicitly for
reproducible analyses, for example with
`load_data("AgingMouse", release = "20260711")`.

After required files are cached, `offline = TRUE` prevents network
access.
